:::{#def-logical-connective}
#### Logical connective

A **logical connective** builds a new proposition (@def-proposition)
from one or two propositions $P$ and $Q$,
with a truth value that depends only on the truth values of $P$ and $Q$.
These notes use five, defined next:
not (@def-not), and (@def-and), or (@def-or),
implies (@def-implies), and if and only if (@def-iff).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-not}
#### Not

The logical connective (@def-logical-connective) **not** is written $\neg P$ ("not $P$");
it is true when $P$ is false,
and false when $P$ is true.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-and}
#### And

The logical connective (@def-logical-connective) **and** is written $P \land Q$ ("$P$ and $Q$");
it is true when $P$ and $Q$ are both true,
and false otherwise.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-or}
#### Or

The logical connective (@def-logical-connective) **or** is written $P \lor Q$ ("$P$ or $Q$");
it is true when at least one of $P$ and $Q$ is true,
and false when both are false.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-implies}
#### Implies

The logical connective (@def-logical-connective) **implies** is written $P \Rightarrow Q$ ("if $P$, then $Q$", or "$P$ implies $Q$");
it is false when $P$ is true and $Q$ is false,
and true otherwise.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-iff}
#### If and only if

The logical connective (@def-logical-connective) **if and only if** is written $P \Leftrightarrow Q$ ("$P$ if and only if $Q$");
it is true when $P$ and $Q$ have the same truth value,
and false otherwise.

:::
